item: Four cryptograms (c1, c2a/b, c3, c4a/b)
where_held: Adirondack History Museum / Essex County Historical Society (ECHS; Brewster Memorial Library credit line)
note: The target itself; listed for completeness. Scans also in Farnsworth 2010 and on Cipherbrain 2015

item: Clear French poem "Oh! mes amis je vous supplie en grâce" (14 lines, "No.11. (next page la suite)")
note: No source found (not in Brown 2021). Page numbering "No.11" implies a numbered series of sheets

item: Title "monographe. verse." with bird-and-key monogram, circular banner "HENRY.D.DEBOSNYS" (twice)
note: Drawn sign; no second occurrence found in any public source checked

item: Signature "Hênêcos Debosnostys." + Latin Aeneid V.437-438 under c4b
note: Brown PDF p.6 reproduces the leaf and identifies the Virgil lines (Entellus)

item: Greek poem headed "(Greek translation.)", on the back of c4
note: Moore's Greek preface ode to Anacreon, altered and cut short. Brown PDF p.7 image seems to show an anchor-like mark at one line end (my reading of a small image, unverified)

item: Multilingual sample page (Latin, "Portuguese", French, English, Spanish)
note: Latin = Vulgate Ps 140:4; English = Fordyce "Answer"; Portuguese not real Portuguese; Spanish only partly visible

item: Second pseudo-language text "inno calledaz / Ontro de palade mosa kaen falei ..."
note: Not identified as any language; possibly invented. Worth a look as a possible cipher/argot specimen

item: Poem "The Valley of the death"
note: Moore patchwork (6 sources). Garvey 1989 snippet also names it with the 29 Aug 1882 date

item: Poem "The Solitary grave, Or the hermit dying alone"
note: Stoddart, The Death-Wake (1831); signed "-Henry Debosnys.-"

item: Poem "The City of the Death"
note: Moore patchwork plus original lines ("go meet my poor wife into death")

item: Poem "Our Last Meeting"
note: Moore

item: Poem to "my dear Celestine" ("March 5, 1882")
note: Chivers, "To Isa in Heaven"; names an earlier wife, "Celestine"

item: Kind Words verse
note: Colesworthy

item: Quatrain "Why do we vainly weep at fate"
note: Moore, Anacreon Ode XXXVI; signed "Henry D. Debosnys"

item: Verse "She died like golden insect in the dew"
note: Stoddart; signed "Husband H. Debosnys, Elizabethtown"

item: Total poem count: "twenty-five poems he wrote in jail"
